                     WABASH VALLEY POWER ASSOCIATION, INC.
                     REQUEST FOR ISSUANCE OF AN ERRATA


To the Commission:

           On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued its “Order Instituting Proceeding Under

Section 206 of the Federal Power Act” in this above captioned proceeding.1 In its Order,

the Commission found that Midcontinent Independent System Operator Inc.’s (“MISO”)

existing Open Access Transmission, Energy, and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff

(“Tariff”) appears to be unjust, unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory or preferential and

thereafter directed MISO and thirty (30) Participating Transmission Owners (“PTOs”)

within MISO to show cause with respect to a variety of concerns related to large load or

co-located load transmission and interconnection within sixty (60) days of the date of its

Order.2 Wabash Valley Power Association, Inc. (“WVPA”) has identified a procedural

issue with the Order and respectfully requests that the Commission issue an errata as soon

as practicable.

           Before addressing the procedural issue presented below, WVPA desires to clarify

that it does not dispute the need for the Commission to address issues surrounding service

to large load and co-located load within organized markets and elsewhere. Further, WVPA

acknowledges the Commission’s existing precedent regarding non-jurisdictional entities



1
 Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., et al, 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 (June 18, 2026) (the

 with certain rate schedules within a jurisdictional RTO or ISO.

          The Commission included WVPA as one of the PTOs in the caption of the Order.

However, at footnote 11 of the Order, the Commission described which PTOs it intended

to include in the caption and made clear:

                Transmission Owners refers to the entities listed in the caption
                of this order. We recognize that MISO’s transmission owners
                include entities that are not subject to the Commission’s
                jurisdiction because they are not public utilities pursuant to
                section 201(f) of the FPA. See 16 U.S.C. § 824(f); Sw. Power
                Pool, Inc., 180 FERC ¶ 61,022, at PP 44-45 (2022).
                Accordingly, the Commission has not included 1803 Electric
                Cooperative, Inc.; Ames Municipal Electric System; Arkansas

                Springfield, Illinois City Water and Light Plant of the City of
                Jonesboro; Cooperative Energy; Dairyland Power

                Inc.; Indiana Municipal Power Agency; Lafayette City-Parish
                Consolidated Government; Michigan Public Power Agency;
                Michigan South Central Power Agency; Minnesota Municipal
                Power Agency; Missouri Joint Municipal Electric Utility
                Commission; Missouri River Energy Services; Municipal
                Electric Utility of the City of Cedar Falls, Iowa; Municipal
                Energy Agency of Nebraska; Prairie Power, Inc.; Rochester
                Public Utilities; Sam Houston Electric Cooperative, Inc.;
                Southern Illinois Power Cooperative; Southern Minnesota
                Municipal Power Agency; Willmar Municipal Utilities; and
                WPPI Energy here as Transmission Owners that must respond
                to this order to show cause. Nonetheless, the Commission
                retains the authority to review each entity’s formula rates as a
                component of MISO’s Tariff in an order to show cause directed
                towards MISO, and MISO must respond to this order regarding
                the non-public utilities’ MISO Tariff provisions on file with
                                               3

                      the Commission. See Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 180 FERC ¶
                     61,022 at P 40.[3]

           Like each of the PTO entities listed in footnote 11, WVPA is not a public utility

pursuant to section 201(f) of the FPA. In January 2025 WVPA informed the Commission

that as a result of the termination of one of its members, it ceased to be a public utility on

January 1, 2025 because it became exempt from the Federal Power Act as a result of being

wholly owned by exempt entities. As of January 1, 2025, WVPA has been wholly owned

by twenty-one electric cooperatives that receive financing under the Rural Electrification

Act of 1936 or sell less than four (4) million megawatt hours annually and by one additional

member which is wholly owned by WVPA. The Commission subsequently acknowledged

WVPA’s acceptance of its withdrawal of jurisdictional rate schedules based on the change

in status.4

           As of today, WVPA is still wholly owned by electric cooperatives that receive

financing under the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 or sell less than four (4) million

megawatt hours annually and by the additional member it wholly owns. In fact, WVPA is

itself in the process of receiving financing under the Rural Electrification Act of 1936.

WVPA is a PTO within MISO, however, it is a PTO that is similarly situated to all of the

other non-jurisdictional entities listed in footnote 11 of the Order. WVPA respectfully

submits that it is unaware of any basis, stated within the Order or any facts external to the

 Wabash Valley Power Ass’n, Inc., Docket No. ER25-838-000, (Feb. 12, 2025) (delegated order);

                                                 4
7607303
 Order, to treat WVPA any different. WVPA believes that the Order inadvertently identified

it based on its prior status as a public utility.

          In addition, WVPA believes the Commission did not intend to include it as a named

respondent. In the Show Cause Order issued to the California Independent System Operator

(“CAISO”) and its transmission owners in Docket No. EL26-71-000, non-jurisdictional

utilities were purposefully included as respondents “because their Transmission Owner

Tariffs on file with the Commission detail the wholesale load interconnection process in

CAISO.”5 The Commission explained that “[i]f a non-public utility wishes to be removed

from this proceeding, we will rescind the show cause order against them at their request,

and we expect CAISO to respond to this order regarding the non-public utility’s CAISO

Tariff provisions on file with the Commission.”6 The Commission did not express a similar

concern with respect to MISO’s non-jurisdictional transmission owners.

          As the Commission’s interests are in modifying the terms and conditions of the

MISO Tariff, an errata to the Order affecting MISO would not impact or diminish the

Commission’s stated show cause goals. Further, an errata to the Order would be consistent

with the Commission’s treatment of a request from a similarly situated non-jurisdictional

entity in Docket No. EL26-72-000 regarding the Show Cause Order issued to ISO New

England Inc.7 Based on these facts, WVPA respectfully requests that the Commission

 issue an errata to the Order that:

          (1) removes WVPA from the caption of Docket No. EL26-70-000, which intended
              to identify only MISO and jurisdictional PTOs; and

          (2) adds WVPA in the list of non-jurisdictional PTO entities in footnote 11.


          If the Commission determines that the requested corrections exceed the scope of

an errata, WVPA respectfully requests in the alternative that the Commission rescind the

Order with respect to WVPA as described in the CAISO Order precedent, as set forth

above.
